claims.claim: Reviewers report that the prologue and its content have been removed or shortened in a recent update, replacing sections with a quick summary or exposition dump.

citations.review_text: I finished this game on Playstation 5 about a year ago and I loved it. My favorite part about it was the prologue. It was my favorite prologue out of any game I've ever played. It felt so calm sitting down at the house overlooking the land below while talking with Spike. I liked the peace and quiet after the chaotic chase sequence. I was so excited to replay the prologue on PC with higher graphics settings but then I realized THEY HAD REMOVED A HUGE PART OF THE PROLOGUE. Are you kidding me??? There was already an option to skip the prologue. I am genuinely upset that THE DEVELOPERS HAVE CHOSEN TO OUTRIGHT REMOVE CONTENT without any way of getting it back. I will change my review if the developers release an update that adds this content back because this is outrageous.

I recently bought DL2 because it was on sale and i heard in recent years that they made it better since launch.
So i started it up and was surprised that i could not play the prologue since they completly removed it in the last update. Now the prologue/tutorial feels very rushed and akward and rather than experiencing the story you just get a exposition dump.

there also seem to have been other entirely negative changes to the game.
as for me i will downgrade the game to a better version.

problem is is i love this game alot, same with DL1 and while i do recommend it to others im gonna have to give it a negative review due to some changes ive found out about thats happened in the past year including gutting the prologue, removing a fan favorite character from the intro and only mentioning them, essentially removing the prologue in favor of shorting it so you can "get to the action sooner" even though the game features a button to skip the prologue, theyve also censored a scene in the intro where the protagonist almost gets lynched and apparently there might be more cuts or changes like it in the future, while i love the Dying Light series to death i cannot advocate for the changes they are making as they are ruining the vibes, atmosphere, and story telling of the game, personally dont know if it has anything to do with Techland being bought by Tencent or not or if there was any racial motivation in the changes (due to Tencent being a Chinese company there are accusations of racism with the change as they removed a prominent black character that returns from DL1 and they added an optional skin that changes another black character into a Chinese character and made it enabled by default from what ive heard) there is also potential evidence of Tencent, Techland, or some third-party botting reviews for Dying Light 2 in response to waves of negative reviews for the game, unless they revert the change i cannot in good faith give this game a positive review

First of all, I paid for this game. Dear developers (And Tencent..), how would you feel if you went to a restaurant, paid for a three-course meal, and then someone walked over and took away your appetizer?

I previously played this game on another platform, but I put it on hold because of technical issues. Now I've bought it again, only to discover that the prologue has been removed... from a STORY driven game.

Your explanation was:

"We've refined the prologue to be shorter and more engaging, letting players dive into the core of the game quicker."

No, what you actually did was replace it with a one-minute recap video and remove roughly 30 minutes of interesting gameplay, all under the justification that new players should get into the game faster.

Why wasn't there simply an option to skip the prologue?
Add a "Skip Prologue" button. Players who don't care about story or played the game before it can skip it and watch the summary video if they want. Everyone else can experience the original prologue, immerse themselves in the world, get to know the characters, and enjoy the proper setup for the story.

I genuinely cannot understand how removing part of the game was considered a good idea.

Please restore the prologue's deleted content, the prologue for me is one of the best parts of the game, i just don't understand what are you guys doing or thinking by changing parts of a story that is already done 4 years ago? removing chunks of a game for absolutely no reason at all like the hanging scene that you decided to censor in an older patch. Will update my review when you guys fix this. 

Edit: They updated the game, and did not restore what's been deleted in the prologue still. 
What a disappointment!

claims.claim: The game opens with promotional trailers and advertisements for DLC or other games directly in the main menu.

citations.review_text:
I have not been this uninterested in a game in a long time. Dying Light 2 felt soulless and boring in every way possible.

The first impression is already awful. Every time you launch the game, you are pushed through trailers or promotional screens. Yes, intros can be disabled in the settings, but why spam them every time the game is opened?

The main menu looks like mobile game slop, which is reinforced by the fact that there is in-game currency in a single player game (60€ btw). You can also buy DLC that gives you sci-fi armor and a laser rifle. Great for post-apocalyptic immersion...

Before you can even play co-op, you have to sit through a long prologue and tutorial that takes around 2-3 hours before you can properly play with a friend. The timing feels suspiciously convenient considering Steam’s 2 hour refund window 🤔

While my game was installing, my friend tried the tutorial, and it was everything you would expect. It treats you like an idiot the entire time, constantly holding your hand and explaining basic things like you have zero clue. I eventually downloaded a save file from Nexus just to bypass the intro and get straight into co-op.

Once I finally got into the actual game, it did not get better. We started on Nightmare because we wanted a challenge, but the zombies were a joke. During free roam and the first mission, we were both running and jumping around without alerting anything, then walking up to zombies from behind or even from the front and pressing "F" for takedowns. This repeated with dozens of zombies. It felt completely brainless. Human enemies were not much better. Their melee attacks felt broken because once they started an attack, they seemed to latch onto you for a guaranteed hit, which was more annoying than difficult.

The UI and inventory system are horrible. Everything looks cluttered, ugly, and unpleasant to use. It does not feel clean, immersive, or satisfying.

The performance and visuals are somehow even worse. I have a high end…

I barely played it but seriously, they replaced the realistic physics based zombie movements with fixed animations? This feels like some early 2000s game, I don't know how to explain it, but for anyone who's played GTA San Andreas, where you attack someone and they don't react with physics they do a fixed animation? That's kinda what it's like... Sometimes the animation doesn't even seem to match the move you made, you kick the zombie and it jerks like crazy or falls weirdly(because it's not physics, it's just a falling animation...). Not to mention your movements feel exaggerated and over the top, in an unrealistic way... 

The voice acting is worse, the tutorials are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ annoying teaching you basic things about the game and you have to hold space for like 5 seconds to close it. I skipped the prologue thinking i would be able to avoid these tutorials. 

I won't make this too long, but lastly, the menu literally starts with a video playing a trailer for the DLC? Seriously? I hate when games put "trailers" for DLC or other games in their menu, it's fine if it's like a button on the side but why is it so in your face "buy our DLC please!" 

As someone who loved the first one and heard bad things about this one but wanted to give it a chance... needless to say, i wouldn't recommend this... I'm probably gonna download the first one again and play it rather than play this hunk of trash.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that updates removed portions of the starting prologue, replacing important context and character interactions with condensed cutscenes or black screens.

citations.review_text:
Can't play the entire product I payed for because they removed the first hour of the games prologue. This then turns the current first hour into a bit of a confusing mess. 

You make your way through an area that feels it should be much more open, meet some guy you are told is a contact of a friend you never see only for him to die, run away from a weird group you have no context for and meet some guy who walks you to an empty box and leave you to die as night time all of a sudden happens after cutscene. No world building just a mess that say "hey, uhh go to the hospital, you don't really know why but trust us".

Also as a side note the game is still way too dark and cutscenes where your flashlight turns off is basically a black screen even with gamma all the way up which only ends up washing out the screen once you can see.

I hate leaving a negative review for this because the game itself is genuinely great.

The gameplay is incredibly fun, the world is beautiful and the parkour feels so much better than it did back at launch. Combat is satisfying, this is still the best open world zombie experience out there and overall the game has aged surprisingly well.

Unfortunately all of that gets overshadowed by one baffling decision.

Sometime after Tencent got involved Techland completely butchered the first hour of the game. When you launch a new save it asks if you'd like to skip the prologue. Sounds reasonable, right? Except if you choose No it still skips most of the prologue anyway. Around 30-40 minutes of content is just gone. Several iconic cutscenes and memorable sequences have been removed entirely for no good reason.

The weirdest part is the censorship.

At the end of the prologue, when you first enter the Bazaar, the locals try to hang Aidan. This used to be a full cutscene and it was one of the most memorable introductions in the game. Now the entire sequence is literally just a black screen before the game continues.

This is a game where you can decapitate people, cave in skulls and spill intestines but apparently showing someone being threatened with hanging was too much? It's such an absurd contradiction that I honestly thought my game had bugged out the first time I saw it.

If this was done because of Tencent or to satisfy some censorship requirements then it's a terrible change. If it wasn't, then I genuinely have no idea what Techland was thinking.

The game is still fantastic but preserving a classic should mean preserving it, not quietly cutting out pieces of it years later. That's the only reason this review is negative.
Completely ruined the setup for the game by removing basically the entire prologue for literally no reason

I'm only writing this review as backlash to a horrible decision.

  I wanted to properly play through the game and get into it, so I restarted with a new save as a clean slate, instead of 13 hours in with little to no memory. When I began the prologue, I immediately felt something was off, with a cutscene barely stretching over a minute that crushes a lot of exposition into it. I looked up if something was changed, and found the near 40 minute prologue, filled with character dynamics, important story, and a reason for the protagonist, was all removed in favor of said cutscene and the tail end walk to the city.

  I cannot express enough how much I felt the urge to close the game once the cutscene was over. It felt like watching a recap of a show's previous episode and not the crucial beginning to a game's story. They even removed an entire character, returning from the first game, and relegated him to a single referring line he doesn't even say.

  And the irony in all this? There's an option to skip the prologue and watch a condensed cutscene with a quick tutorial. How can you even condense it further than 40 minutes into a 1 minute cutscene?!
lots of fun, a huge upgrade from the first game. bit disappointed to know they shortened the prologue.
They literally just removed parts of the game, years after release....

Gutting the prologue - removing conversation with Spike at the start made me lose all intrest in giving this game a second chance, i'll probably do it just so my friend can gain all the achievements but truth be told I don't want to even turn it on. I've wanted to play more of this game when I bought new PC that could handle it but now it seems pointless, from what i watched on yt the story is mediocre at best and now without important context we were given from Spike it lost it's spark completely. Overall it was the most idiotic decision Techland could've made and as a Pole it hurts my heart that they did that. Juicy middle finger and justice for Spike, bring the OG prologue back.
Removed the prologue for no damn reason (there was already a skip option)

I went into this game expecting a good sequel.

I left wondering how I accidentally spent hours just running across rooftops instead of progressing the story.

I only played the main campaign (haven't touched the side quests yet), and honestly... it was epic from beginning to end. The story kept me invested the whole way through, and I genuinely wanted to see how Aiden's journey would end.

But let's be honest...

The real star of the game is the movement.

Parkouring across rooftops, climbing skyscrapers, using the grappling hook to launch yourself across the city, chaining vaults into wall runs... it's ridiculously satisfying. After a while you stop using the streets because the rooftops become your second home.

The melee combat is also incredibly fun. Smashing zombies off buildings, kicking enemies into spikes, and improvising your way through fights never gets old.

And the views...

♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.

Standing on top of a skyscraper and looking across the city, watching the sunset, seeing nature slowly reclaim what's left of civilization...

It's genuinely beautiful.

There were multiple moments where I completely forgot about the objective and just stood there looking at the scenery.

Few games make me do that.

I also loved the ending I got. Being able to save Mia after everything Aiden went through was incredibly satisfying. And seeing Lawan choose to leave Villedor behind and walk away with Aiden instead of staying there, even leaving Frank and everyone else behind,was the perfect conclusion for me. After everything those two had been through, they deserved to leave that city together and finally have a chance at a new beginning. 

And also Even though Aiden did absolutely everything he could to save Mia, it genuinely hit me seeing her die shortly after escaping X13. After everything he sacrificed and everything he went through just to find her, watching her pass away anyway was heartbreaking. At least she got to see the outside world one last time.

10/10
Best Parkour animations I've ever seen just overall a great game

I don't get why people dislike Dying Light 2 Stay Human. When I began playing, I had a lot of fun and really enjoyed it. I love the parkour mechanics and the different movement options, especially the dropkick. The graphics are stunning. The world-building and level design are impressive, and I really like the weapon designs. The story is average. Dying Light had a better storyline. But overall, the gameplay is a blast. For me, it's a 8.5/10 game.

This game is SO MUCH WORSE than the first game, I was barely having fun. After 12 hours the game decided to soft lock me in a misson and I will NOT start from the beginning.
Anyway, here's a list of things I noticed before the soft lock.

-Headshots either deal no extra damage, or it is so minimal you won't even notice.
-Guns are almost impossible to find, but ammo is abundant.
-Weapons look and feel weak.
-The world is empty and moving around is slow.
-The parkour is not only weak, but really glitchy at times.

Dying Light 2 took everything that made the original game enjoyable and decided it would be fun to downgrade mostly everything. Instead of a grappling gun we got a rope you can swing from, instead of cool guns you can get in the main story, we got a bow and arrow. The only way to obtain guns in this game (something you can easily obtain in the first game) is to either purchase pre-built weapons from the in-game store using real money or by doing an obscure side quest that you need to complete WEEKLY and DAILY mission bounties to continue unlocking and purchasing guns. This game made guns obtainable by putting them in side content rather than through mainline story progression for seemingly no reason other than perhaps to increase sales through their in-game store with real life money, I don't see any other reason why that would be the case. The story is all over the place, the game feels like it has no clear direction while simultaneously having one clear goal. Characters in this game come and go and almost every single character feels like they're expendable and have no real plot relevance after a single mission. Most of my enjoyment of this game comes solely from the co-op gameplay and even then, when you are not the host, this game has it's fair share of bugs whether it be clipping through elevators or simply not being able to enter plot relevant areas with the host and being forced to teleport to the host once they reach a specific checkpoint. Overall, for a sequel to a good co-op zombie game, I am pretty disappointed. The ending of the game was all over the place, it felt as if it was bringing characters back randomly as if the game creators forgot they existed until the last moment just to add them back like "aha, they're still here, we didn't forget about them!". As a sequel this game is a disappointment to what I expected of a sequel to Dying Light; if this were a standalone game rather than a sequel, I would say this game is okay, the combat can be fun, the…

Very mediocre experience that feels like a downgrade in a lot of ways over the previous game, lots of bugs and coop had some issues but its by far the best way to play the game. For example, i couldn't respawn when i died so every time i die i have to either wait for my friend to revive me or wait 40 seconds and then every time we need to progress the story by entering a door not only do we BOTH need to interact with the majority of doors but then the game has the audacity to make that stupid paraglider tutorial mission a SLOG to get through because every time Lawan moves away 50 meters and you go to her its another cutscene and that happens 3 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ TIMES. I was soft locked once in an elevator and i don't know if its a bug or what but in a stealth mission guards would react strangely to the coins thrown sometimes not even reacting to them. Stealth is a useless mechanic because its only used for stuff like dark places where virals are sleeping and even then its faster to kill them than stealth past them. Kicking feels WAY weaker with only the dropkick and the one for kicking enemies heads when they're downed being a useful skills for combat with all the others in parkour and combat being impractical like the bash or the jump off of enemies. The story is mostly a "go here do that here's what you'll do" with the ending being severely disappointing AND EVEN SKIPPING ITSELF SO WE HAD TO WATCH IT ON YOUTUBE. NOT ONLY THAT but the choices you have in most dialogue are all illusions of choice, where it doesn't really matter what you choose because there's only one right answer. If only steam had a rating for mediocre, but because its 5/10 i won't give it a negative review as its not a bad game but its not good either.

So i loved the first game and was really looking forward to the  second game but was severley dissapointed and frustrated by the bugs and inconsistency's of the gameplay. If i closed out the game in a building, i would spawn in its walls or under the building. when doing parkour, my character would land on a vehical and die, not grab a ledge and die, or land on a thin platfrom and slide off and die. When it came to combat i would activate a perfect dodge (slow mo) and still get hit by the attack no matter the direction dodged. Dying Light 2 took everything that made the original game enjoyable and decided it would be fun to downgrade mostly everything. Instead of a grappling gun we got a rope you can swing from, instead of cool guns you can get in the main story, we got a bow and arrow. The only way to obtain guns in this game (something you can easily obtain in the first game) is to either purchase pre-built weapons from the in-game store using real money or by doing an obscure side quest that you need to complete WEEKLY and DAILY mission bounties to continue unlocking and purchasing guns. This game made guns obtainable by putting them in side content rather than through mainline story progression for seemingly no reason other than perhaps to increase sales through their in-game store with real life money, I don't see any other reason why that would be the case. The story is all over the place, the game feels like it has no clear direction while simultaneously having one clear goal. Characters in this game come and go and almost every single character feels like they're expendable and have no real plot relevance after a single mission. Most of my enjoyment of this game comes solely from the co-op gameplay and even then, when you are not the host, this game has it's fair share of bugs whether it be clipping through elevators or simply not being able to enter plot relevant areas with the host and being forced to teleport to the host once they reach a specific checkpoint. Let me start off by saying I actually love this game and it really sucks to not recommend it and leave a negative review. However, this recent patch (10/06/2026) is beyond awful. It is abysmal. 

This update had been hyped over the course of 3 days in the Dying Light official discord and with the game being in its final year of support people were excited. Unfortunately the update has come with some of the worst set of patch notes I've seen in my years of gaming;

- Prologue has been 'refined' - as in gutted. No longer is Spike in the game and you begin at the radio tower. This removes a LOT of context from the story and will confuse new players.
- A £35 DL pack and a 'welcome' bundle when the game has been out since 2022 with a Kyle Crane skin which is a recolour of the one from the Outbreak event.
- A redone UI that focuses more on the in-game shop than the game itself.
- The shortest bare minimum of fixes possible when the game is crying out for bug fixes lasting years.
- Bugged out textures and skins, such as the Kyle Crane The Beast skin from the Outbreak event. Maybe to get people to buy the bundle version?
- Hyped up community maps which have been around for years? Why?
- Mod support but the mods are buggy and don't always work.
- More pointless bounty grind for recoloured items/outfits.

For someone like me who only got the game last Christmas as a gift and never followed the painful growth of Dying Light 2 and it's MANY iterations throughout the years, I find this distasteful, dull and frankly insulting. I can't imagine how long time players feel about this. 'Refining' the prologue - which can be SKIPPED by the way - butchers the whole point of the game.

I'm very disappointed in Techland and I hope they reverse this awful update. Until then this game is staying fixed in it's current state thanks to tech magic, where it will never be spoiled by this god awful decision.

PSA - do not update this game if you want it to be less than you wanted.

overall its hard to deny that its up there with the best zombie games that exists. The atmospohere, the fights with melee weapons, the world.. it delivers. The intense chases at night , cornered in some dark facility.. just you and your weapon slashing thru whatever comes for you and popping flare in the last moment to show volitailes that in fact you are the apex predator,   not the other way around .  Just make sure to REPLACE LAWAN with snake makeover skin, its pain to watch story otherwise. Be ready for some bugs, some immersion breaking unlogical things every now and then. Damage is lacking, ammo is chore to get , you cannot reload while sprinting, it wont stun the zombies. Probably the biggest annoyance is limits of items in inventory , so you often face a choice to suit up only few weapons you will use. For example if you want to have one or two mags for each firearms , there’s no space for arrows . And if you want to have many arrows / or different types, there’s no space for bullets. Opposed to first game that had set limit for each gun, here the limit is set for all the guns and items. You can’t have all the boosters on hand either , just a few types. 

Make sure to turn DX 12 and ray tracing and all that eye candy, its well needed graphical upgrade from 1st game.

Dying Light 2: Death by a Thousand Menus (And Inconsistent Parkour)

TL;DR: At the end of the day, Dying Light 2 is pure Eurojank. Despite the shiny new coat of paint and some fun puzzle mechanics, a lot of the exact same structural issues that plagued Dead Island 1 over a decade ago are still alive and well here. If you value consistent gameplay and smooth combat flow, this one will just piss you off.

I went into Dying Light 2 really wanting to love it. I rolled credits, cleared out the story, and finished all the side quests (though I skipped the 100% collectible grind). I gave the game a completely fair shake. But by the time I reached the end, my goodwill was completely exhausted. What starts as a promising zombie parkour sandbox slowly devolves into an exercise in pure frustration.

The Good: Puzzles and Picking

Let's start with the bright spots. The lockpicking mechanic is perfect, absolutely no notes. Don't change what's not broken.

The game also does a surprisingly good job with the power cable puzzles. The base game’s metro generators would have been fantastic if they had just a little more variety (they all start to feel exactly the same after a while), but the DLC nailed the execution. The cable plus generator combos in the DLC were perfectly balanced and genuinely fun to figure out.

The Bad: UI, Inventory, and Shattered Game Flow

The menu UI and inventory management are actively fighting against you having fun. You can't just easily equip your best gear; you are forced to back all the way out of every menu just to make simple changes.

Combat flow is constantly broken by arbitrary limits. Throwing knives cap at 99 in a slot, meaning when you inevitably run out, you have to pause the game or wrestle with the clunky weapon wheel mid-fight just to restock. The ammo economy is equally baffling. You find tons of ammo but no actual guns, and the game’s strict capacity limits force you to make tedious, time-wasting trips back to your stash just to manage i…

I’ve genuinely tried to give this game THREE separate chances over the past years because I loved the first game, and somehow every single time I come back it feels even worse.

First of all: co-op progress not carrying over into your own world is one of the dumbest design decisions I’ve seen. Spending hours playing with friends just to return to your solo save and realizing almost nothing counted just makes no fkn sense.

The whole region assignment system is stupid. You permanently lock yourself into choices that barely feel rewarding anyway. Combat skills feel insignificant for most of the game and  it takes like 40+ hours before the Combat is SOMEWHAT enjoyable.

The story sucks balls. The game constantly jumps between quests with new characters so fast you forget what the actual plot is even about. It’s just cutscene after cutscene after fkn cutscene (with MAYBE 10 seconds of pressing W  in between) :DDD

The gameplay is absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Dodging feels inconsistent, the paraglider is horribly executed, and the grappling hook somehow feels worse than the one from the first game. Everything about it just feels so clunky i can't even describe how ass it actually is^^ 

Nightrunner trials are a pure ragebait and trying to 100% this game is one of the least fun completion experiences I’ve had in a while.

What makes it worse is that the game had a horrible release, still needs fixing in sooo many ways, and instead of actually fixing this game first, they just give us a third game while completely abandoning the storyline from this part and jumping back to the original characters from DL1???

Overall the game feels rushed, frustrating, and nowhere near as good as the first Dying Light.

The only good feature I can think of is the Steam game profile since it gives a clean background if you spend 10k points on it. I probably had more fun customizing my profile than actually playing thi…

The gameplay is a nice improvement from the first game, but the story is so bad it makes me think it's bad on purpose. By the end of the game I was already skipping cutscenes because the writing is so awful and cringy I couldn't take it. I did not care about any of the characters or anything that was going on in the world.

Still, it's a nice playground to kill some zombies in and remains the best parkour game IMO. The map is huge and the sense of freedom is pretty cool. It makes me think of what could it have been if they had more time to add different random events, because even though the map is big, the encounters are all basically the same.

Long story short, it's not worth it at full price, but it's a good game.

Dying Light 2: Death by a Thousand Menus (And Inconsistent Parkour)

TL;DR: At the end of the day, Dying Light 2 is pure Eurojank. Despite the shiny new coat of paint and some fun puzzle mechanics, a lot of the exact same structural issues that plagued Dead Island 1 over a decade ago are still alive and well here. If you value consistent gameplay and smooth combat flow, this one will just piss you off.

I went into Dying Light 2 really wanting to love it. I rolled credits, cleared out the story, and finished all the side quests (though I skipped the 100% collectible grind). I gave the game a completely fair shake. But by the time I reached the end, my goodwill was completely exhausted. What starts as a promising zombie parkour sandbox slowly devolves into an exercise in pure frustration.

The Good: Puzzles and Picking

Let's start with the bright spots. The lockpicking mechanic is perfect, absolutely no notes. Don't change what's not broken.

The game also does a surprisingly good job with the power cable puzzles. The base game’s metro generators would have been fantastic if they had just a little more variety (they all start to feel exactly the same after a while), but the DLC nailed the execution. The cable plus generator combos in the DLC were perfectly balanced and genuinely fun to figure out.

The Bad: UI, Inventory, and Shattered Game Flow

The menu UI and inventory management are actively fighting against you having fun. You can't just easily equip your best gear; you are forced to back all the way out of every menu just to make simple changes.

Combat flow is constantly broken by arbitrary limits. Throwing knives cap at 99 in a slot, meaning when you inevitably run out, you have to pause the game or wrestle with the clunky weapon wheel mid-fight just to restock. claims.claim: Reviewers praise the parkour system, describing movement, rooftop traversal, and fluid mechanics as a major highlight of the game.

citations.review_text:
Dying Light 2: Stay Human is an open-world action survival game developed by Techland. As the sequel to Dying Light, it expands on the original game's parkour and combat systems while introducing a larger world and a choice-driven story.

The game follows Aiden Caldwell, a survivor searching for information about his past in a world devastated by a zombie virus. His journey takes him to The City, one of the last major human settlements, where different factions compete for power and control.

One of the game's strongest features is its improved parkour system. Players can climb skyscrapers, swing across rooftops, and move through the city with incredible freedom. Traversing the environment feels smooth and satisfying, making exploration one of the most enjoyable aspects of the game.

Combat has also been expanded with new abilities, weapons, and skill trees. Players can choose different approaches, whether focusing on melee combat, agility, or stealth. The battles are fast-paced and exciting, especially when facing large groups of infected.

A major addition is the choice-based narrative. Decisions made throughout the story can affect factions, missions, and parts of the city itself. This gives players a greater sense of control and encourages replayability.

Visually, the game is impressive. The detailed city, dynamic weather, and lighting effects create a believable post-apocalyptic world. The day-night cycle returns as well, with nighttime becoming significantly more dangerous due to stronger infected roaming the streets.

However, the story is sometimes inconsistent, and some choices have less impact than expected. The game also suffered from technical issues at launch, although many have been improved through updates.

Overall, Dying Light 2: Stay Human successfully builds upon the foundation of the first game. Its excellent parkour, engaging combat, and vast open world make it a great experience for fans of action and zombie survival games.

Rating: 8.5/10

Dying Light 2: Reloaded Edition is a game that shines brightest when you stop focusing on the story and just enjoy running across rooftops while smashing zombies in the face.
The parkour system is easily the best part of the game. Moving through the city feels smooth, fast, and incredibly satisfying once you unlock more movement abilities. Chaining jumps, wall-runs, glides, and grapples together makes traversal genuinely fun even after dozens of hours.

Combat is also enjoyable, especially once you start getting stronger weapons and upgrades. Sending infected flying off rooftops never really gets old, and nighttime exploration creates some genuinely tense moments when stronger infected start chasing you through the streets.

Compared to launch, the Reloaded Edition feels much more polished and feature-complete. A lot of improvements and updates helped make the overall experience better, especially for co-op and combat. 

The good:
- Excellent parkour and movement system
- Traversal feels incredibly satisfying
- Fun and brutal melee combat
- Great co-op experience
- Large open world with lots to explore
- Nighttime gameplay creates real tension
- Tons of weapons, upgrades, and gear
- Visuals and city design are impressive
- Much improved compared to launch
- Dropkicking zombies remains amazing

The bad:
- Main story is pretty forgettable
- Dialogue and characters are inconsistent
- RPG loot system can feel unnecessary
- Open-world activities become repetitive
- Choices don’t impact the world as much as advertised
- Combat can feel floaty at times
- Some animations and physics feel awkward
- Bugs still occasionally happen
- Endgame grind can become tedious

Overall, Dying Light 2 is at its best when it fully embraces being a parkour zombie sandbox. The story may not leave a huge impact, but the movement, co-op gameplay, and chaotic nighttime exploration make it a very fun open-world experience.

Dying Light is one of my favorite games, the first was a sleeper hit and while this one had a rocky start, its now to the same level as the first game! Parkour + Zombies with some of the smoothest gameplay and movement around!

UPDATE:

I have played and loved all of the entries, HOWEVER. I am removing my positive review given the most recent update. The studio that produced this franchise, Techland, was acquired by Chinese company Tencent a few years ago. This made many long term fans uneasy because Tencent has a less than stellar reputation in the gaming industry... for soon to be obvious reasons.

There have been a few questionable choices over the past year (Mainly an addon skin that race-swaps one of the main characters, Lawan, from black to asian. WEIRD.) culminating in an update today, 6/10/2026. The games original prologue was surprisingly poignant and sets the stage as a bleak and empty yet oddly beautiful world, with one of the characters from the previous game (Spike, a black man) catching us up to speed on the 15 year timeskip between Dl1 and Dl2. This cutscene was widely seen as the best part of the games storyline, which released to mixed reviews.

As of today, this prologue has been COMPLETELY gutted. What once was a playable tutorial is now a Marvel Studios-esque intro cutscene, with the one of the main changes being that Spike is now no longer a voiced character, and is only mentioned once in the game with a less than 2 second clip.

There was NO discernable reason for this change to be implemented, and as of now it smacks very obviously of racism. Overall this change leaves a VERY bad taste in my mouth and makes me worried about the future of this franchise.

Had a lot of fun with this game. The parkour, combat, shooting, and overall gameplay loop were the highlights for me. Running around the city and taking on enemies never really got old.

The story was enjoyable to follow, even though it had some cliches and rough moments, especially after reaching the main city. It wasn't anything groundbreaking, but it was still a fun ride with some memorable moments.

One downside is that Techland has basically moved away from actively supporting the game. There are still occasional updates and random events, but it doesn't feel like the game has much of a future anymore. Not a huge fan of that, but it is what it is.

Overall, come for the gameplay. The parkour, combat, and open-world experience are where this game shines. The story is alright and adds to the experience, but the gameplay is the real reason to play.
